description: FIRST FEATURE-TREE GOLDEN: the feature-tree design's §6 worked example — a 40 x 25 mm rectangle sketched on the XY datum plane (4 lines, the doc's 5 constraints, entities at the analytic positions) extruded 10 mm additively. Locks the full evaluate-tree path: planegcs sketch solve → profile wire assembly + closed-wire check → face → prism along the plane normal → GProp on the evaluated body → tessellation → content-addressed GLB (mesh_glb_id). The sketch is deliberately underconstrained (§6 has no anchor; DOF 10) with zero initial residual, so the solver provably returns the input positions bitwise — solver determinism is asserted by the harness determinism gates through the same model. Since the materials slice (2026-07-30) the model also assigns a DOCUMENT material (aluminium 6061), so this golden additionally locks the mass path: mass = volume x density, computed beside the volume it is derived from, and a centre of mass that for a single-material body coincides exactly with the volume centroid. Every OTHER golden assigns no material and therefore asserts the opposite half of the contract -- mass reported as ABSENT, never 0 g.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug).

profile: the §6 rectangle spans x in [0,40], y in [0,25] on XY; entities start at the analytic solution and the 5 §6 constraints have zero residual there, so the solved profile is exactly the drawn rectangle (verified bitwise 2026-07-11, planegcs 0.8.0: solved == input, status underconstrained, DOF 10)
volume = 40 * 25 * 10 = 10000 mm^3 (profile area 1000 mm^2 x 10 mm depth)
centroid = (40/2, 25/2, 10/2) = (20, 12.5, 5) mm by symmetry; extrude direction 'normal' on XY is +Z, so z spans [0, 10]

mass = volume x density = 10000 mm^3 x 2700 kg/m^3 = 10000 x 2700e-6 g/mm^3 = 27.0 g EXACTLY (aluminium 6061, py_kit.schemas.materials: 2700 kg/m^3 = 2.70 g/cm^3, and 10000 mm^3 = 10 cm^3). Hand-derived from the analytic volume above, never recorded from output. Measured deviation: 3.6e-15 g.

center_of_mass = (20, 12.5, 5) mm -- identical to the volume centroid, because one body of one material is homogeneous and the density factors out of the weighted integral. Mass weighting only diverges from volume weighting when bodies of DIFFERENT densities combine (see the multibody-two-disjoint-boxes golden). Measured deviation: <= 3.6e-15 mm.
bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[40,25,10]: sketch coordinates are world X/Y on the XY datum plane, prism along +Z

topology: a rectangular prism is 6 planar faces, 12 straight edges, 1 closed shell — same counts as the primitive box golden, but built via BRepBuilderAPI_MakeFace + MakePrism instead of BRepPrimAPI_MakeBox

mesh: each planar rectangular face tessellates to exactly 2 triangles (6 * 2 = 12); faceted per-face normals mean no vertex sharing across faces, so 6 faces * 4 corners = 24 vertices (same convention as box-10x20x30)

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). Unlike the primitive box (exact 0.0), the wire->face->prism construction path accumulates ulp-scale floating-point error in GProp's integration over the constructed planar faces. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-11, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume 1.82e-12 mm^3 (~2e-16 relative, one-ulp scale at 1e4), surface_area exactly 0.0, centroid <= 3.6e-15 mm, AABB exactly 0.0 on all six bounds. Documented ceiling 1e-9 = ~500x the observed worst case, headroom for libm/platform variation across CI hosts — while staying 100x TIGHTER than the standing planar 1e-7 bound, matching the cylinder golden's posture. The solver contributes zero error by construction (zero-residual start, solved == input bitwise). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md. Mass and centre of mass ride this same bound rather than one of their own: mass = volume x density and every library density is < 1 expressed in g/mm^3 (aluminium 6061 is 2.7e-3), so the propagated mass error is strictly SMALLER than the volume error already bounded here -- measured 3.6e-15 g on mass and <= 3.6e-15 mm on the centre of mass (2026-07-30), ~2.8e5x inside the 1e-9 ceiling.
